newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian activists hold East Timor vigil.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian activists hold East Timor vigil.

text.p: The families of some dozen Malaysian human rights activists detained during a conference on East Timor held a candlelight vigil on Tuesday night outside a police station.

The detainees were among over 60 Malaysian activists and journalists rounded up on Saturday after a mob of youths, comprising groups allied to the Malaysian government, forcibly shut down the conference.
A further 46 foreign participants, including two Roman Catholic bishops, were deported.

The Asia Pacific Conference on East Timor (APCET II), a collection of human rights groups, was called to draw international attention to the plight of the former Portuguese colony invaded by Indonesia in 1976.
The conferemce was condemned by Kuala Lumpur as damaging to its relations with Indonesia.
Indonesia has ruled East Timor in defiance of the United Nations, which has never recognised Jakarta's 1976 annexation of the territory.
Seven of the several hundred people who stormed the conference, overturning furniture and berating the activists, were detained and released several hours later.
APCET on Tuesday renewed a call for the remaining activists' release from what it described as "appalling conditions" in the police station. It was not clear exactly how many were still detained.
It said three of the detainees had been sent to hospital, two suffering asthma attacks.
APCET said the remaining detainees could be held until Thursday, when they would have to be released or have their remand periods extended.
